newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam reports signs of trade gap narrowing.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam reports signs of trade gap narrowing.

text.p: Vietnam reported signs on Wednesday of a narrowing of its trade gap, and said exports during the first five months of this year were expected to register an increase of almost 32 percent.
Data released by the State Statistics Office showed exports for May were seen reaching $720 million against imports of $950 million.

Exports during the first five months of this year were seen reaching $3.36 billion and imports $4.49 billion, giving a resultant trade deficit of $1.13 billion compared to $1.87 billion recorded between January 1 and May 10 last year.
In a report accompanying the figures, the Statistics Office said the main export growth was seen in commodities, including rubber, coffee, tea, rice and crude oil.
Imports were seen rising just 1.5 percent against their levels a year ago. The main imports were petroleum products, fertilizer and goods for the foreign-invested sector.
Vietnam's trade gap has become a major concern for the communist country. In 1996, the deficit reached $4.0 billion, equivalent to an unsustainable 17 percent of Gross Domestic Product.

Swedish economists warned in a recent report that Hanoi urgently needed to reform its trade policies and cautioned against resorting to import substitution measures as a means of tackling its deficit.
It said Vietnam would have to take active export promotion measures using efficient exchange rate policies.
The Statistics Office also reported on Wednesday that Vietnam's industrial growth for the first five months of 1997 was expected to have grown 13.7 percent compared to the same period in 1996.
It said the state owned sector was seen growing 11.1 percent, the non-state sector 10.6 percent and foreign invested 22.8 percent.
